harbor_antrieb_executor.summary:
Implemented, via an Ansible playbook run from node4 (the pre-baked Ansible control appliance), a topology where node2 serves an app on TCP/8080 reachable by node3 only through a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1 (VyOS). node1/node2 share a private L2 segment (node1 eth1 = 10.10.10.1/24, node2 enp8s0 = 10.10.10.2/24). node3, which only sits on the shared management network, reaches that private segment exclusively via a WireGuard tunnel: node1 wg0 = 10.10.20.1/24 listening on its management-network IP (UDP 51820), node3 wg0 = 10.10.20.2/24, with node3's AllowedIPs routing 10.10.10.0/24 and 10.10.20.0/24 through the tunnel. node2's app binds only to its private IP (not 0.0.0.0) and firewalld's internal zone restricts tcp/8080 to the private+tunnel subnets, so node2:8080 is unreachable from the shared management network, from node4, or from node3 except through node1's tunnel. Verified end-to-end: curl from node3 to 10.10.10.2:8080 succeeds via the tunnel; curl to node2's public IP:8080 and from node4 both fail (connection refused/timeout, nothing listening there).

Root-caused and fixed a VyOS-specific Ansible/SSH issue along the way: running `configure`/`set`/`commit` as the `vyos` SSH user silently failed to persist any config (my_cli_bin logged "without config session" and commit reported "No configuration changes") even though session env vars looked correct, while running the identical script as root succeeded — fixed by enabling Ansible `become`/passwordless-sudo for the VyOS host group. Also discovered and cleared 8 leaked unionfs-fuse config-session mounts under /opt/vyatta/config/tmp left behind by earlier interactive debugging attempts, which was blocking new session creation.

Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id plus service/tunnel/app evidence) on all 4 managed nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, and node4 one at a time via `systemctl reboot` (backgrounded with a short delay so the acknowledgement returned before the connection dropped), polled each node until exec access returned, confirmed a changed boot_id for every node, and verified full recovery afterward: node1's eth1/wg0 interfaces and WireGuard handshake with node3 came back automatically; node2's private IP, static route, app systemd service, and firewalld internal-zone rule all persisted and the app served correctly again; node3's wg-quick@wg0 tunnel re-established and the app remained reachable through it; node4's Ansible control files, SSH key, and connectivity to all three other nodes were intact and `ansible -m ping` succeeded against all hosts post-reboot.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology via exec: node1=VyOS (dual NIC, eth0 on shared mgmt net, eth1 unconfigured second NIC), node2/node3=RHEL10 (node2 has a second private NIC enp8s0, node3 single NIC), node4=Ubuntu with a pre-baked Ansible control appliance (ansible-core, collections, baked SSH key, run.sh/build-image.sh confirming its role)

Distributed the cluster SSH keypair: added CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY to node2/node3 root authorized_keys and to node1's vyos user via native VyOS `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys` config; installed CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY on node4
Wrote /root/inventory.ini on node4 grouping node1 (vyos user), node2/node3 (root), overriding the default ansible.cfg remote_user/key

Authored /root/playbook.yml on node4: generates WireGuard keypairs on node1 and node3 (idempotent, no_log), configures node1's eth1 private IP and wg0 (address/port/private-key/peer) via native VyOS CLI commands wrapped in script-template + configure/commit/save, configures node3's wg-quick@wg0 via a rendered wg0.conf and installs wireguard-tools, configures node2's private static IP + route to the WireGuard subnet via community.general.nmcli, deploys a systemd-managed python http.server bound to node2's private IP only, and restricts tcp/8080 via a dedicated firewalld internal zone rich-rule scoped to the private+tunnel subnets

Debugged and root-caused a VyOS config-session failure when run as the vyos SSH user (fixed by enabling Ansible become/sudo for the VyOS host group) and cleared 8 stale unionfs-fuse session mounts left over from debugging
Fixed a missed task: added the node1 eth1 private-IP `set` command to the VyOS apply task (it was omitted in the first working pass), re-ran the playbook, and confirmed end-to-end reachability
Verified end-to-end functionality (tunnel-only reachability, direct-path and node4 bypass both fail) before and after the restart protocol

Executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on all 4 managed nodes sequentially: baseline capture (boot_id + service/tunnel/app health), backgrounded systemctl reboot with ack-before-disconnect, poll-to-recovery, boot_id-change verification, and post-restart health/data verification for each node in turn

evidence.requirement: App served from node2 on TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: node2 shows LISTEN on 10.10.10.2:8080 via the node2-app systemd service; curl from node3 over the tunnel returns the app's HTML content pre- and post-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 reaches node2:8080 only through the WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1
evidence.summary: node3 wg0 shows an established handshake with node1 (public key oxmpRw12...=/kwtGRC7...=) and a route to 10.10.10.0/24 via wg0; curl to node2's private IP succeeds only via that route, while direct curl to node2's public IP (10.100.81.11:8080) and from node4 both return HTTP 000 (no listener reachable)

node4's pre-baked ansible-core control node ran /root/playbook.yml against /root/inventory.ini (node1/node2/node3), syntax-checked, pinged all hosts, and completed successfully (ok/changed, 0 failed) across two full runs including the eth1 fix

evidence.requirement: Only the configured control node used for orchestration
evidence.summary: Confirmed node4 (not node1/2/3) is the purpose-built Ansible control appliance (ansible-core pre-installed, run.sh/build-image.sh referencing EXECUTED_FILE/inventory.ini workflow) and used it exclusively to orchestrate the other three nodes over SSH

evidence.requirement: Node1 baseline capture and restart evidence
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5bcff8f9-... with healthy wg0/eth1/forwarding captured; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id changed to 3f385428-...; eth1, wg0, and the WireGuard handshake with node3 all recovered automatically

evidence.requirement: Node2 baseline capture and restart evidence
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f455a75c-... with active app/listener captured; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id changed to ae0f559d-...; private IP, static route, app service, firewalld internal zone, and app response all recovered

evidence.requirement: Node3 baseline capture and restart evidence
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 368725cb-... with active tunnel captured; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id changed to b27a2b23-...; wg-quick@wg0 tunnel re-established (new handshake) and app remained reachable through it

evidence.requirement: Node4 baseline capture and restart evidence
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d3d54083-... with intact Ansible control files captured; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id changed to 43015728-...; playbook/inventory/SSH key intact and `ansible -m ping` succeeded against node1/node2/node3 afterward
